name: Will My Los Angeles County Building Receive a Mandatory Seismic Retrofit Order?

mainEntity.name: How can a Los Angeles County building owner tell if their older soft-story or mixed-use building will receive a mandatory seismic retrofit order in the next few years?
mainEntity.text: How can a Los Angeles County building owner tell if their older soft-story or mixed-use building will receive a mandatory seismic retrofit order in the next few years?

acceptedAnswer.text: Predicting whether a building will receive a mandatory seismic retrofit order in Los Angeles County requires a combination of jurisdiction research and basic structural screening. Owners should start by confirming the year of original construction and any major structural alterations; buildings from before the late 1970s are much more likely to be target candidates, especially if they are soft-story or non-ductile concrete. Next, identify your jurisdiction: City of Los Angeles, another incorporated city, or unincorporated County. Jurisdictions with soft-story or non-ductile concrete ordinances often publish building lists, maps, or parcel lookups of structures that are expected to receive or have already received retrofit notices. If your building appears on these inventories, a compliance order is likely. Visually, soft-story and mixed-use buildings with large open front parking, tuck-under parking, or extensive ground-floor storefront openings beneath multiple residential stories are typical soft-story candidates. Mixed-use or apartment buildings with a weak or flexible first story and minimal shear walls often fall under these programs. If you suspect your building configuration and age match ordinance criteria, consider a preliminary evaluation by a structural engineer or experienced seismic retrofit contractor. They can confirm whether your structure fits current definitions and whether your city is planning to expand its retrofit program. This proactive assessment helps you anticipate mandatory orders and plan financing, tenant communication, and construction timing before deadlines tighten.
acceptedAnswer.description: A Los Angeles County owner can gauge retrofit risk by checking the building’s age, structural type, location, and listing on any published soft-story or non-ductile concrete inventories. Buildings built before modern seismic codes, with open ground floors or weak first stories, in jurisdictions with soft-story ordinances are the most likely to receive mandatory retrofit orders.
